purpose: Behavioral evaluations for autonomous Roblox scene-lighting creation, reconstruction, implementation, and validation.

evals.prompt: Create the lighting for a cozy Roblox social cafe with large windows, warm wood, pastel furniture, an outdoor garden, and a minimum target of older phones. Make it inviting without washing out UI or making the garden unreadable.
evals.expected_output: A map-aware lighting thesis, explicit assumptions, a valid lighting plan, quality tiers, a Studio-ready implementation path, and gameplay/accessibility validation. Numeric settings are labeled as starting hypotheses rather than universal values.
assertions: Selects FROM_SCRATCH without requesting information already present.
Explains visual hierarchy and interior/exterior balance before choosing effects.
Uses restrained bloom and color grading rather than effects as the primary light source.
Includes a mobile fallback and tests UI, player silhouettes, entrances, and the garden route.
Produces or offers machine-actionable lighting-plan.json and Luau when filesystem tools are available.

evals.prompt: Match this single Roblox gameplay screenshot as closely as possible. It has a purple dusk sky, long shadows, blue fog in the distance, warm lamps, and strong glowing signs. I do not know the original settings.
evals.expected_output: An observation ledger that separates evidence from hypotheses, estimates parameter ranges and confidence, identifies camera/material confounders, generates competing hypotheses if needed, and follows dependency-ordered iteration instead of guessing exact hidden settings.
assertions: Selects MATCH_SCREENSHOT.
Does not claim to recover exact source properties from one image.
Analyzes sun direction, shadow length/softness, ambient fill, atmosphere, local lights, emissives, exposure, grading, bloom, and camera/FOV cues.
Separates lighting mismatch from geometry, materials, textures, and camera response.
Specifies at least one high-information additional view while still completing a best-effort first pass.

evals.prompt: Use this screenshot and https://www.roblox.com/games/1234567890/example-game to recreate the game's lighting in my own map. Find more public gameplay screenshots with the same lighting condition before deciding the settings.
evals.expected_output: Public-only Roblox research, a source ledger, candidate media grouped/ranked by likely lighting state, authenticity and recency caveats, visual confirmation, then confidence-aware screenshot reconstruction.
assertions: Extracts the place ID and attempts current public place-to-universe, metadata, media, and thumbnail sources when tools permit.
Supplements official media with web/image search queries when useful.
Ranks or clusters candidates by broad appearance but visually verifies map/state identity before treating them as evidence.
Treats promotional thumbnails as potentially staged, edited, or outdated.
Never requests cookies, bypasses authentication, or claims access to the game's source settings.

evals.prompt: My Roblox horror game is atmospheric but testers keep getting lost and say everything is black. Improve it without removing the horror mood. The player carries a flashlight and enemies must remain fair.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that preserves darkness as composition rather than clipping, a hierarchy of safe dark values and focal pools, flashlight/local-light guidance, fairness tests, and a staged validation plan.
assertions: Does not solve the problem by globally over-brightening the map.
Checks crushed blacks, ambient fill, exposure, materials, fog, and display/quality differences.
Uses contrast, silhouettes, landmarks, practical lights, and route rhythm to guide players.
Tests enemy telegraphs and hazards at minimum quality and on dim/bright displays.
Avoids making critical information depend only on hue or bloom.

evals.prompt: Audit and optimize the lighting for a competitive Roblox FPS. We have many shadowed PointLights in an industrial map, frame drops on mobile, and players complain that opponents disappear in doorways.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-led audit that preserves competitive fairness, reduces expensive overlapping/shadowed local lights, distinguishes official facts from heuristics, and defines device/quality tests and profiler gates.
assertions: Prioritizes stable enemy silhouettes and doorway adaptation over cinematic darkness.
Audits light range, overlap, shadow use, activation, CastShadow, geometry, post effects, and quality behavior.
Recommends measurement with Studio profiling/device tools instead of asserting a universal light-count budget.
Creates explicit low, medium, and high quality behavior.
Preserves art direction through practical fixtures, baked-looking emissive cues, and selective hero lights.

evals.prompt: This old tutorial tells me to set Lighting.Technology to Future and tweak Outlines. Update my place to the modern Roblox lighting system and explain what is deprecated.
evals.expected_output: A current-API migration that flags deprecated or legacy properties, uses current LightingStyle and supported controls where appropriate, and avoids inventing writable behavior for restricted rollout properties.
assertions: Flags Technology and Outlines as legacy/deprecated rather than blindly scripting them.
Checks current official Roblox documentation before making time-sensitive API claims when web access exists.
Explains visual intent and maps it to current supported properties/instances.
Provides a safe backup and staged comparison workflow.
Does not promise one-to-one visual parity across renderer changes.

evals.prompt: My render is much brighter and shinier than the reference even though ClockTime, Brightness, and Atmosphere match. Make the lighting match from these two screenshots.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that checks camera/FOV/exposure, sky cubemap, environment specular response, SurfaceAppearance/MaterialVariant data, geometry normals, and post-processing before compensating with arbitrary global lighting changes.
assertions: Does not assume the difference is only Lighting service values.
Compares camera and silhouette alignment before pixel/color metrics.
Checks PBR roughness/metalness and EnvironmentSpecularScale.
Masks or excludes UI and unrelated scene differences from comparison.
Changes one dependency family at a time and records the result.

evals.prompt: Design realistic rainy-night lighting for my Roblox city. You cannot access Studio, but give me everything needed to implement it safely.
evals.expected_output: A valid plan, generated Studio-ready Luau, manual placement instructions for semantic local-light targets, rollback script, assumptions, and a visual/device validation checklist.
assertions: Proceeds without asking for Studio access.
Creates a non-destructive implementation plan with a unique plan ID.
Separates global Lighting objects from Camera-local effects.
Includes warnings for unresolved target paths and external assets.
Explains what could not be visually verified without running the place.

evals.prompt: You have Studio access. Copy this bright stylized simulator screenshot into my open place and replace the existing lighting setup, but make it reversible.
evals.expected_output: A pre-edit audit, backup, explicit conflict-replacement decision, tagged managed instances, staged implementation, comparison captures, quality/gameplay validation, and tested rollback.
assertions: Audits current Lighting, Terrain Clouds, post effects, local lights, runtime scripts, and camera effects before editing.
Backs up affected state and preserves a restoration path before replacement.
Does not delete unrelated content without recording and backing it up.
Captures matched-camera before/after images and documents residual differences.
Tests rollback in the working session or clearly reports if the capability is unavailable.

evals.prompt: Copy the lighting from this cinematic showcase screenshot into a fast obby. Keep the same mood, but gameplay readability matters more than exact pixels.
evals.expected_output: A style-transfer interpretation that identifies which visible traits can be preserved and which cinematic effects must be reduced or localized for motion, navigation, and low-quality resilience.
assertions: Labels the objective as gameplay adaptation rather than exact pixel matching.
Preserves palette, sun/sky relationship, atmospheric depth, and focal rhythm where feasible.
Reduces or gates blur, depth of field, extreme bloom, crushed blacks, and distracting SunRays.
Tests jumps, hazards, moving camera, checkpoints, and failure/retry loops.
Documents intentional deviations from the reference and why they improve play.
